items.prompt: What does the abbreviation SEO stand for?

options.label: Search element ordering
Search engine optimization
Secure engine operations
Site engagement optimization

rubric: SEO means search engine optimization, the practice of earning organic traffic.
Other options are invented expansions that sound plausible.

items.prompt: Which HTML element sets the title that usually appears as the clickable headline of a result on a search results page?

options.label: `<title>`
`<aside>`
`<footer>`
`<script>`

rubric: The `<title>` element in the head is typically used as the result headline.
Other elements are valid HTML but do not define the page title.

items.prompt: What is a backlink in SEO?

options.label: A link from your page to another page on your own site
A link from another website that points to a page on your site
A link from a page on your site that points to a page on another website
A link in your browser that returns you to the previous page

rubric: A backlink is an inbound link from an external site to yours.
Distractors describe internal links, browser navigation, or outbound links.

items.prompt: Which file, placed at the root of a site, tells crawlers which paths they should not crawl?

options.label: `robots.txt`
`sitemap.xml`
`favicon.ico`
`style.css`

rubric: `robots.txt` holds crawl rules for bots.
`sitemap.xml` lists URLs to help discovery, not to block crawling.

items.prompt: What are organic search results?

options.label: Unpaid listings that the search engine ranks by relevance
Results that only come from social media posts and shares
Results shown because an advertiser paid for the placement
Results that a site owner chooses to feature on the page

rubric: Organic results are unpaid listings ranked by the engine's algorithm.
Paid placements are ads, which are a separate category.

items.prompt: Which of the following are on-page SEO elements that you control directly in a page's own content or HTML? Select all that apply.

options.label: Backlinks from other websites
Heading tags such as `<h1>`
Meta description
Title tag
Domain registrar choice

rubric: Title tags, meta descriptions and headings are on-page elements edited in the page itself.
Backlinks are off-page signals, and the registrar is not an on-page element.

items.prompt: A small shop owner has just launched a new website with many product pages. She wants to give search engines a single file that lists the URLs she wants them to find. Which file should she create and submit?

options.label: A 404 page
An XML sitemap
A canonical tag
A robots.txt file

rubric: An XML sitemap lists URLs to help search engines discover pages.
A robots.txt file sets crawling rules rather than listing URLs to find, and a 404 page or a canonical tag does not list URLs either.

items.prompt: Why do search engines treat backlinks from reputable, relevant sites as a positive ranking signal?

options.label: They make the linked page load faster for visitors who arrive from the referring site
They act like endorsements that suggest the page is trustworthy
They prove the linked page was written by a qualified professional author
They automatically add more keywords to the linked page

rubric: Links work as votes of trust from other sites.
Distractors confuse links with speed, keyword content or authorship proof.

items.prompt: A user searches for "buy running shoes size 10 online". Which search intent does this query most clearly show?

options.label: Transactional, being ready to make a purchase
Informational, wanting to learn how shoes are made
Navigational, wanting to reach one specific brand's homepage
Local, wanting directions to a nearby store

rubric: Words like "buy" and a specific size signal a purchase intent.
Other intents do not match the wording of the query.

items.prompt: Why are long-tail keywords such as "waterproof trail running shoes for wide feet" often a good target for a new site?

options.label: They usually get more searches than short keywords, so traffic is higher
They face less competition and show more specific user intent
They do not need any relevant content on the page
Competitors ignore them because the phrases are too long to rank for

rubric: Long-tail phrases have lower competition and clearer intent.
They usually have lower search volume, and they still need relevant content.

items.prompt: Which of these tasks is best classified as technical SEO rather than content or link building?

options.label: Compressing images so pages load faster
Asking another site to link to your guide
Writing a new blog post for a target keyword
Posting an article summary on social media

rubric: Page speed work concerns site infrastructure, which is technical SEO.
The others are content creation, link building and promotion.

items.prompt: A site owner adds a `noindex` robots meta tag to a page and the search engine recrawls it. What is the most likely outcome?

options.label: The page stays but loses all of its backlinks
The page ranks higher because it is marked clearly
The page is dropped from the search results
The page is crawled less often but stays in the results

rubric: `noindex` asks engines to keep the page out of their index.
It does not boost rankings or remove links, and it does not just reduce crawling.

items.prompt: Why is keyword stuffing, repeating a target phrase unnaturally many times, a poor SEO practice? Select all that apply.

options.label: It makes the text hard and unpleasant for people to read
It deletes the backlinks that point to the page
It makes the browser fail to render the HTML
It is treated by search engines as an attempt to manipulate rankings

rubric: Stuffing harms readability and looks like spam to search engines.
It does not affect backlinks or break HTML rendering.

items.prompt: A bakery's website shows the same cake page at two URLs: one with a tracking parameter and one without. The owner worries that search engines will see duplicate content. What does adding a canonical tag to both pages do?

options.label: It redirects visitors from the parameter URL to the clean URL
It merges the two pages into one file on the server
It blocks crawlers from visiting the parameter URL at all
It tells search engines which URL to prefer for indexing

rubric: A canonical tag names the preferred URL among duplicates.
It does not block crawling, hide pages from visitors or merge files.

items.prompt: What is the main job of a page's meta description in SEO?

options.label: To tell crawlers exactly which keywords the page should rank for in results
To summarize the page in search results so searchers are persuaded to click
To list every keyword that visitors might use to find the page online
To set the headline shown on the browser tab and in the results listing

rubric: The meta description is the snippet text that can win clicks; it is not a keyword list.
Distractors confuse it with the title tag or with the outdated keywords meta tag.

items.prompt: Why does a link from a trusted, relevant website help a page rank?

options.label: It passes the linking site's keywords to your page, so your own topical relevance rises
It works as an endorsement of the page, and endorsements from respected sources count for more
It lets the crawler fetch your page faster, so it is indexed within seconds of the link going live
It increases how often people search for your brand name, so your rankings rise as a direct result

rubric: Search engines treat links as endorsements, weighted by trust and relevance.
Distractors treat links as a crawling shortcut or a keyword transfer, which they are not.

items.prompt: Which search query most clearly shows informational intent?

options.label: white sneakers sale near me
buy white sneakers online
StrideCo white sneakers price
how to clean white sneakers

rubric: 'How to' queries signal the searcher wants to learn something.
The other queries show buying or comparison intent.

items.prompt: What is the difference between crawling and indexing?

options.label: Crawling is used for paid listings; indexing is used for organic listings in results
Crawling discovers and fetches pages; indexing stores them so they can appear in results
Crawling orders pages by quality; indexing counts the links pointing to each one
Crawling stores pages in a database; indexing discovers and fetches new pages by following links

rubric: Crawlers find and fetch pages; indexing stores and organises them for retrieval.
The strongest distractor reverses the two steps.

items.prompt: A page has `<meta name='robots' content='noindex'>` in its head and crawlers can reach it. What will most likely happen?

options.label: The page ranks lower but still appears for searches of its exact title
The page is hidden from visitors but is still listed in search results
Crawlers can still fetch it, but search engines leave it out of results
Crawlers are blocked from fetching it, so the page is never visited at all

rubric: Noindex tells search engines not to list the page; crawlers must be able to fetch it to read the tag.
Distractors confuse noindex with blocking crawling or with a ranking demotion.

items.prompt: Which of these are on-page SEO elements you control directly on a page? Select all that apply.

options.label: Heading structure (H1, H2)
Image alt text
Title tag
Number of backlinks from other sites
Age of the domain registration

rubric: On-page elements are edited within the page itself: titles, headings and alt text.
Backlinks come from other sites and domain age is not editable, so both are off-page or external factors.

items.prompt: A florist's site has two separate pages, one called 'Wedding Cakes' and one called 'Wedding Cake Ideas', both written to rank for 'wedding cakes'. Neither page ranks well. What is the most likely explanation?

options.label: The pages compete for one query, splitting signals so neither ranks as well as one strong page
Search engines merge near-identical pages on a site automatically, so rankings consolidate with no action needed
Repeating a target keyword across pages triggers a manual penalty that removes the whole site from results
Only one page per site can be indexed for any query, so the second page is ignored by search engines

rubric: Keyword cannibalization splits relevance and link signals between pages targeting the same query.
Distractors invent automatic merging, penalties or a one-page-per-query limit.

items.prompt: You are writing the title tag for a page selling women's red running shoes from the brand StrideCo. Which title best follows good practice?

options.label: Shoes | StrideCo Online Store | Page 1 of the Catalogue
Women's Red Running Shoes | Free Returns | StrideCo
Welcome to the Official StrideCo Website Home Page Today
Red Shoes, Running Shoes, Women Shoes, Cheap Shoes, Buy Shoes

rubric: A good title puts the specific topic first, stays concise and adds the brand naturally.
Distractors are vague, keyword-stuffed or generic.

items.prompt: You are permanently moving a guide from `/old-guide` to `/new-guide` and want to keep its search ranking signals. What should you do?

options.label: Set a 302 redirect from /old-guide to /new-guide
Set a 301 redirect from /old-guide to /new-guide
Keep both pages live with the same text on each
Delete /old-guide and let visitors reach a 404 page

rubric: A 301 marks a permanent move and passes signals to the new URL.
A 302 signals a temporary move; a 404 or duplicate pages lose or split signals.

items.prompt: A new online shop selling laptop accessories wants its first keyword target to bring sales soon. Which keyword is the best pick?

options.label: 'laptop': 500,000 searches, very high difficulty, mixed intent, big brands dominate results
'laptop sleeve review videos': 900 searches, medium difficulty, research intent
'buy leather laptop sleeve 13 inch': 300 searches, low difficulty, purchase intent
'history of laptops': 5,000 searches, low difficulty, informational intent

rubric: Low difficulty and purchase intent suit a new site that wants sales.
Distractors chase raw volume or ignore commercial intent.

items.prompt: The same shoe page loads at both `/shoes` and `/shoes?color=red` with identical content. You want search engines to treat `/shoes` as the main version. What should you add?

options.label: `<link rel='canonical' href='https://example.com/shoes'>` on /shoes?color=red
`<a rel='nofollow' href='/shoes'>` on /shoes?color=red
`<link rel='canonical' href='https://example.com/shoes?color=red'>` on both URLs
`<meta name='robots' content='noindex'>` on /shoes

rubric: The canonical tag on the duplicate should point to the preferred URL.
Noindex on /shoes would remove the main page; canonicalising to the parameter URL picks the wrong version.

items.prompt: A product page shows a photo of a woman jogging on a trail in red StrideCo running shoes. Which alt text is best?

options.label: Woman jogging along a trail wearing red StrideCo running shoes
Woman jogging on a trail in red StrideCo running shoes, buy StrideCo shoes today
StrideCo running shoes red running shoes trail shoes women jogging shoes cheap
woman-jogging-trail-red-strideco-running-shoes-photo-large.jpg

rubric: Good alt text describes the image accurately and naturally for users and search engines.
Distractors are keyword stuffing, a filename or vague filler.

items.prompt: A blog post targets 'how to repot a cactus'. Which edits follow on-page best practice? Select all that apply.

options.label: Repeat the exact phrase in every sentence to raise density
Put the phrase naturally in the title tag and the H1
Use 'click here' as the anchor text for all internal links
Link from related posts using descriptive anchor text such as 'cactus soil guide'
Write a unique meta description that summarizes the repotting steps

rubric: Natural keyword placement, descriptive internal anchors and a unique meta description are standard on-page practice.
Keyword repetition and 'click here' anchors are stuffing and wasted context.

items.prompt: A site audit of a small online shop shows 40 product pages all use the title 'Product | Shop'. The owner can make one fix this week. Which fix should you apply first?

options.label: Buy backlinks pointing at the product pages so their duplicated titles are ignored
Write a unique title for each page using the product name and a key attribute
Add extra keywords to the homepage title so the shop looks broader to search engines
Apply noindex to the product pages until the shop's category pages start to rank

rubric: Unique, descriptive titles let each product page target its own query.
Distractors ignore the cause or remove pages from results instead of fixing titles.

items.prompt: A shop wants to rank for the query "buy trail running shoes women". Which existing page best matches the intent behind that query?

options.label: A category page of women's trail shoes with filters
A blog post on the history of trail running races
The homepage with the brand story and founder interview
A how-to article on training plans for new trail runners

rubric: The query is transactional, so a product listing page fits the intent.
Distractors are informational or brand pages that do not serve a buying query.

items.prompt: A product page is reachable at /shoe and at /shoe?color=red, with near-identical content. Which fix applies the standard approach to consolidate the duplicates?

options.label: Add rel=canonical on the parameter URLs pointing to the clean product URL
Redirect the clean product URL to the colour parameter version permanently
Block the clean product URL in robots.txt to avoid duplicate content
Add noindex to the clean product URL so only the variants are indexed

rubric: A canonical tag on the variants tells search engines which URL to index.
The other options remove or demote the preferred URL instead of consolidating signals.

items.prompt: You are writing the title tag for a recipe page targeting "vegan lasagna recipe" on the site Greens Kitchen. Which title follows good practice?

options.label: Home | Greens Kitchen | Welcome to our site about food and cooking
Vegan Lasagna Recipe: Easy Dairy-Free Dinner | Greens Kitchen
Recipe, Recipes, Vegan Recipes, Lasagna Recipes, Vegan Lasagna Dinner
Greens Kitchen's Very Best Ever Amazing Vegan Lasagna Recipe for Dinner Tonight

rubric: Good titles put the main keyword early, stay roughly under 60 characters and are unique and descriptive.
Distractors stuff keywords, run too long or ignore the target keyword.

items.prompt: A blog post moves permanently from /blog/old-post to /articles/new-post. Which setup best passes its ranking signals to the new URL?

options.label: Meta refresh after 10 seconds to the new URL
Delete the old URL and return a 404 status
301 redirect from the old URL to the new URL
302 redirect from the old URL to the new URL

rubric: A 301 signals a permanent move and consolidates signals on the new URL.
A 302 signals a temporary move; 404s and delayed refreshes lose or weaken signals.

items.prompt: In a blog post you are linking to your page that walks through how to check a site for crawl errors, broken links and slow templates. Which anchor text best applies internal linking practice?

options.label: https://example.com/p?id=482
technical SEO audit checklist
SEO, best SEO, SEO tips, SEO tools, SEO services
our guide to improving your website overall

rubric: Descriptive anchor text tells users and crawlers what the target page covers.
Generic, raw-URL or mismatched anchors give little or misleading context.

items.prompt: A product page ranks at position 8 for "standing desk" and has only a 150-word description. Which on-page changes apply sound practice? Select all that apply.

options.label: Add sections answering common questions such as height range and weight capacity
Repeat "standing desk" 40 times in the description
Write descriptive alt text for each product image
Add extra keywords in white text on a white background
Copy the manufacturer's description that every other retailer uses

rubric: Helpful, unique content and descriptive alt text improve relevance and accessibility.
Keyword stuffing, hidden text and duplicated copy are spam or add no value.

items.prompt: A page ranks in position 3 for a keyword with 10,000 searches a month, and position 3 gets about a 10% click-through rate. Your team estimates position 1 gets about 28%. If the page reaches position 1, how many additional monthly visits should you forecast?
rubric: The CTR gain is 18 points, and 18% of 10,000 is 1,800.
2,800 uses the full new CTR, ignoring current traffic; others are miscalculations.

items.prompt: Two weeks after launching a redesigned site, organic traffic fell 90%. A crawl shows every page returns 200 and carries a meta robots "noindex, nofollow" tag that was absent on the old site. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: Staging-site noindex tags were carried over to the live site at launch
The XML sitemap lacks lastmod dates, so pages were deindexed
Google applied a manual penalty because the URL structure changed
The 301 redirects expired, so all link equity was lost permanently

rubric: A noindex directive on live pages explains the deindexing; staging carry-over is a classic launch error.
Other options do not match the evidence of 200 status codes plus a new noindex tag.

items.prompt: A well-optimised post targeting "best crm software" sits on page 3. The top ten results are all comparison lists of many vendors, while the post is a pitch for one vendor's product. What best explains the ranking?

options.label: The post's format does not match what searchers for this query are shown and want
The post links out to too many external sites, which blocks it from ranking
The post's page is slower than the average of the top ten pages, which prevents ranking
The post's title tag has too few characters to rank against competitors on page one

rubric: When all top results share a format, a different format signals an intent mismatch.
Distractors blame minor on-page or speed factors that do not explain the pattern.

items.prompt: Two posts, "email marketing tips" and "email marketing best practices", swap between positions 7 and 9 every week, and neither reaches the top five. Both cover near-identical subtopics. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: Google's freshness update demotes any post older than twelve months, so both fluctuate
The homepage has too few backlinks, so inner posts cannot hold stable positions
Both posts target the same query, splitting signals so Google alternates between them
Both posts load slowly on mobile, which causes weekly position swaps in results

rubric: Alternating URLs for one query is the signature of keyword cannibalisation.
Other causes would not produce the swapping between two overlapping pages.

items.prompt: A page gained 300 links in one week from unrelated foreign sites, all using the exact anchor "cheap loans", and its rankings then dropped. Which analysis fits best?

options.label: Normal link growth; the drop is coincidental, and acquiring more links like these will restore rankings
Exact-match anchors are ideal, so the drop must come from a delayed indexing update
Links from foreign sites are always ignored, so the drop must come from content alone
Likely a manipulative link pattern; audit the links and disavow if they can't be removed

rubric: Sudden, off-topic, uniform exact-match links look like spam or negative SEO, so audit and disavow.
Distractors treat the links as harmless or beneficial.

items.prompt: A site's Largest Contentful Paint is poor on mobile but fine on desktop. The mobile page's top element is a 3 MB desktop-sized hero image with loading="lazy". What is the best diagnosis?

options.label: Structured data is missing, so mobile pages are crawled and rendered more slowly by Google
The large hero image is lazy-loaded above the fold, delaying the largest element on mobile
The title tag is wider than the mobile screen, which delays rendering of the largest content element
Relative internal link paths make mobile browsers fetch the hero image after the whole page

rubric: An oversized, lazy-loaded above-the-fold image directly delays LCP on slower mobile connections.
Distractors cite factors unrelated to loading the LCP element.

items.prompt: A crawl of a large online shop shows several patterns. Which ones indicate crawl budget being wasted? Select all that apply.

options.label: A calendar widget generates links to endless future dates
Faceted filters create endless combinations of crawlable URLs
Each product page has unique descriptive content
Internal links point through redirect chains of four hops
The XML sitemap lists only canonical URLs returning 200

rubric: Infinite URL spaces and long redirect chains make crawlers spend requests on low-value URLs.
A clean sitemap and unique pages are healthy signs, not waste.

items.prompt: Over three months a guide's Search Console data shows impressions up 150%, clicks up only 5%, and average position down from 4.2 to 9.8. A crawl finds no technical errors. What is the best interpretation?

options.label: The page now appears for many more queries, mostly at low positions, which dilutes average position and CTR
A noindex tag was added recently, which inflates impressions in reports while blocking nearly all clicks
A manual action demoted the page from top results, so impressions rose while clicks should fall to nearly zero
The canonical tag now points to another URL, so impressions are being credited to other pages instead of this one

rubric: Broader query coverage at low positions raises impressions while lowering average position and CTR.
The other options contradict the clean crawl or the continuing click growth.

items.prompt: A product page ranked for its model name until a template update. Now it is absent from results, though it returns 200 and is not blocked. Its source shows `rel=canonical` pointing to the parent category URL. What best explains the drop?

options.label: The update lowered the page's keyword density, so Google demoted it below the category page for the model name
The canonical tag blocks crawling of the product page, so Googlebot can no longer read its content or title tag
The 200 status is overridden by the canonical tag, so Google treats the product page as a soft 404 and removes it
Google treats the category as the preferred version, so the product URL's signals are consolidated there and it drops out

rubric: A canonical to another URL asks Google to index that URL instead, consolidating signals there.
Distractors confuse canonical with crawl blocking, soft 404s or keyword density.

items.prompt: An online store's crawl stats show most Googlebot requests hit filter URLs like `?color=red&sort=price`, and new products take weeks to get indexed. Which diagnosis best fits?

options.label: The XML sitemap is too large, so Google ignores any new URLs that are listed inside it until it is split
Parameter URLs trigger a duplicate content penalty that lowers the ranking of every product page across the site
Crawl requests are consumed by near-duplicate parameter URLs, so new products are discovered and fetched much later
Faceted pages dilute the keyword density of product pages, so Google delays indexing until the copy is rewritten

rubric: Crawl capacity is wasted on low-value URL variations, delaying discovery of important pages.
Distractors invoke a duplicate-content penalty, sitemap size limits or keyword density, none of which match the crawl evidence.

items.prompt: Two posts target 'best running shoes' and 'top running shoes' with the same intent. Search Console shows Google alternating which URL ranks, at positions 14-19, and neither reaches page one. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: Google caps each domain at one result per query, so the second post is held back until the first one is deleted or redirected
The titles differ by only one word, which triggers a manual action for near-duplicate titles and suppresses both pages in results
Synonym phrases are treated as unrelated queries, so each post is judged only against pages that use its own exact phrase
Both pages compete for one intent, splitting links and signals, so Google rotates them and neither gains enough strength

rubric: This is keyword cannibalization: overlapping pages split signals and swap in the results.
Distractors assume a hard one-result cap, a manual action or that Google ignores synonyms.

items.prompt: A client-rendered page shows full content in the browser, yet the URL Inspection rendered screenshot is nearly blank and rankings are weak. The page is indexable and its HTML shell is tiny. Which finding best explains this?

options.label: The scripts are minified, which makes the rendered text unreadable to Googlebot's rendering service when it builds the page
The page is served over HTTP/2, which Googlebot's renderer cannot use to fetch the content scripts for the page
The page's H1 is generated by JavaScript, which Google never executes for headings on any page it crawls
`robots.txt` disallows the `/static/js/` folder, so Googlebot cannot fetch the scripts that build the content

rubric: Blocked script resources stop rendering, so Google sees only the empty shell.
Distractors blame minification, HTTP/2 or JS headings, all of which Google handles.

items.prompt: After a redesign, traffic to old blog posts fell 60% though many had strong backlinks. The team 301-redirected every old URL to the homepage to avoid 404s. Which analysis best explains the loss?

options.label: Redirects to an unrelated page are often treated as soft 404s, so relevance and link equity are not carried over
301 redirects pass no link equity, so any redirect would have caused the same loss for linked posts
Old URLs must return 404 to be dropped, so the redirects kept stale pages in the index with no traffic
The homepage redirects created a loop that stopped Googlebot from reaching the new site's content

rubric: Mass redirects to the homepage lack topical match and are usually treated as soft 404s.
Distractors wrongly claim 301s pass no equity, create loops or require 404s.

items.prompt: A new `/guides/` section is linked from the main menu but has had zero impressions six weeks after launch. Which findings would plausibly explain this? Select all that apply.

options.label: Guides include JSON-LD Article markup
Every guide's `rel=canonical` points to the homepage
URLs use hyphens between words instead of underscores
`robots.txt` contains `Disallow: /guides/`
Pages send an `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header from a server rule

rubric: A noindex header, a canonical to the homepage and a robots disallow each keep pages out of results.
Hyphenated URLs and Article markup are normal practice and do not suppress indexing.

items.prompt: A retailer has `/es-mx/` and `/es-es/` pages. Searchers in Spain often see the Mexico version. Search Console flags 'no return tags': the es-es pages declare hreflang to es-mx, but the es-mx pages declare nothing back. What is the best diagnosis?

options.label: The es-es pages lack a self-referencing canonical, the only requirement for regional targeting to function
hreflang works only in XML sitemaps, so tags in page HTML are discarded and ranking reverts to link strength
Language codes cannot be paired with region codes, so both page sets are merged into one Spanish group
hreflang must be reciprocal, so the one-way declaration is ignored and Google picks the version by itself

rubric: hreflang pairs are only honoured when each page links back to the other.
Distractors misstate where hreflang can live, how codes combine, or what canonicals do.

items.prompt: An outdoor retailer's facets create 400k URLs. Data shows search demand for 'black hiking boots' and 'waterproof hiking boots' but none for combos like 'black size 9 waterproof'. Criteria: keep demand-backed pages rankable and cut crawl waste. Which approach is best?

options.label: Leave all facet URLs indexable and let Google choose which ones are valuable, since crawl budget is rarely a problem
Canonicalise every facet page to the main category so signals consolidate on one page, even those with search demand
Block every facet URL in robots.txt to stop crawl waste at the source, including the demand-backed ones
Index a curated set of demand-backed facets with clean URLs, and noindex or canonicalise the other combinations

rubric: A curated indexable set keeps long-tail demand while limiting low-value URLs.
Distractors either throw away demand-backed pages (canonicalising or blocking every facet) or ignore crawl waste (leaving all 400k URLs indexable).

items.prompt: A two-person team needs link growth that is sustainable, low in penalty risk and relevant to the topic. Which tactic best meets those criteria?

options.label: Buy sponsored posts on high-authority blogs with dofollow links, since paid placements give fast measurable gains
Build a private network of expired domains linking in with varied anchor text so the links look natural
Submit guest posts in bulk with exact-match anchors, because anchor text strongly signals ranking relevance
Publish an original industry data study and pitch it to journalists who cover that field

rubric: Original research earns editorial links that are relevant and low-risk.
Distractors are paid, network or manipulated-anchor schemes that violate link guidelines.

items.prompt: An audit finds four issues and one dev sprint is available. Criteria: most organic revenue protected, fixable within the sprint. Which should be fixed first?

options.label: Title tags slightly over the display length on 200 secondary pages with little traffic
Missing alt text on 30% of blog images that get low-volume image search traffic
A template bug adding `noindex` to category pages that drive 40% of organic revenue
A slow footer widget adding 0.1s to load time on pages that already pass Core Web Vitals

rubric: An accidental noindex on revenue pages is the highest-impact, cheapest fix.
The other issues are minor optimisations with little revenue at stake.

items.prompt: A publisher has 2,000 thin pages from old campaigns. Criteria: remove low-value pages without losing traffic or backlinks. Which approach is best?

options.label: Segment by traffic, links and conversions; 301 or merge pages that have links, and remove the rest
Rewrite each page to 1,500 words, because that length is associated with page one rankings and would lift every page
Noindex every thin page but keep it live, because noindexed pages keep passing link equity to the site indefinitely
Delete every page under 300 words with a 404, because thin content acts as a sitewide quality signal that drags rankings down

rubric: Data-led triage preserves pages with traffic or links and prunes the rest.
Distractors apply blanket word-count rules or assume noindex keeps equity.

items.prompt: A manager proposes raising keyword density to 3% on every page to improve rankings. Which critique is strongest?

options.label: Density matters only in title tags and headings, so the 3% target should be applied there instead of in body content, where repetition is ignored
The plan is sound but 3% is too low, since top-ranking pages need about 5% to beat competitors on exact-match phrases
Density is not a ranking target; topic coverage and intent matching matter more, and forced repetition hurts readability
It would work if applied to the meta keywords tag, because search engines read the target terms there to judge relevance

rubric: No fixed density is a ranking factor; forced repetition risks stuffing and poor reading.
Distractors keep the density myth or rely on the ignored meta keywords tag.

items.prompt: A company will move to a new domain. Which elements make the migration plan sound? Select all that apply.

options.label: Keep redirects live for at least a year and monitor Search Console after launch
Redirect all old URLs to the new homepage to keep the setup simple
Crawl staging to compare titles, canonicals and indexability before launch
Disavow all old backlinks at launch so the new domain starts clean
Map each old URL to its closest new equivalent with a one-to-one 301

rubric: URL-level redirects, pre-launch crawl checks and long-lived redirects protect equity and catch errors.
Homepage redirects and blanket disavows discard relevance and good links.

items.prompt: A new site with few backlinks wants organic leads within six months and has two writers. Criteria: realistic ranking odds, buyer intent and available resources. Which keyword strategy is best?

options.label: Focus on low-volume terms with no commercial intent, since they rank quickly and build a large traffic base
Target specific long-tail, high-intent queries with a linked topic cluster, then expand to competitive terms as authority grows
Delay publishing until a backlink campaign reaches a strong authority score, as content cannot rank without it
Aim every page at the highest-volume head term, since volume decides lead potential and difficulty can be fixed with content

rubric: Long-tail, high-intent targets fit a low-authority site and small team, and can scale up later.
Distractors ignore difficulty, intent or the fact that content can rank before authority peaks.

items.prompt: An ecommerce site's faceted navigation creates millions of crawlable filter URLs. Criteria: protect crawl budget, keep the few facet pages with proven search demand (e.g. 'red running shoes') ranking. Which approach is best?

options.label: Canonicalise facet URLs to the parent category so ranking signals consolidate there and crawlers spend less time on filter pages
Keep demand-backed facets indexable with internal links and self-canonicals; keep other combinations out of links and the index
Block most faceted URLs in robots.txt so crawlers skip filter combinations, and rely on the category page to rank for facet terms
Add noindex to most facets but leave internal links in place, so crawlers still discover products and the filter pages stay out of results

rubric: Selective indexing preserves demand-backed pages while limiting crawl waste on the rest.
Blanket disallow or canonicalisation to the category discards the long-tail facets that should rank.

items.prompt: A consultant says: 'Every spammy backlink found in an audit must go into a disavow file, or rankings will suffer.' Which critique is most accurate?

options.label: Partly wrong, because disavow only works for links from domains with low authority scores, so higher-authority spam must be removed by outreach
Correct, because any low-quality link counts against the site until it is formally disavowed, so audits should disavow every flagged link
Overstated, because Google mostly ignores junk links; disavow suits manual actions or paid-link patterns
Wrong, because disavow files are ignored unless the site has already lost more than half its organic traffic after an update

rubric: Google's systems generally ignore ordinary spam links, so disavow is a targeted tool.
Distractors treat disavow as routine hygiene or invent thresholds.

items.prompt: During a site redesign, a team proposes 301-redirecting all 8,000 retired URLs to the homepage to save mapping time. Criteria: retain relevance signals and link equity from old pages. How should you judge this plan?

options.label: Poor, because 301s should be replaced with 302s so the old URLs stay in the index and keep their equity
Poor, because mass redirects to an unrelated page are often treated as soft 404s
Sound, because the homepage has the most authority, so consolidating every old URL there concentrates link equity
Acceptable, because a 301 always transfers full equity to the target regardless of how related the pages are

rubric: Irrelevant redirect targets lose relevance and may be treated as soft 404s.
Distractors assume a 301 transfers equity regardless of relevance or that 302 is safer.

items.prompt: A content-heavy publisher uses client-side rendering; logged-in dashboards share the codebase. Criteria: reliable indexing of articles, small dev budget. Which option is best?

options.label: Keep client-side rendering everywhere, since Google renders JavaScript so no difference exists
Serve crawlers a separate static copy of the site, which gives the cheapest consistent indexing
Move the entire application, dashboard included, to server rendering before any article work
Server-side render or prerender only the public article templates; leave the dashboard client-rendered

rubric: Rendering only the indexable templates meets the criteria at the lowest cost.
Distractors ignore rendering delays, overspend on non-indexed pages, or risk cloaking.

items.prompt: You must evaluate whether new title templates raise organic clicks on 400 similar product pages, in a seasonal business. Which test design is most credible?

options.label: Change all pages and compare to the same weeks last year, since year-on-year comparison cancels seasonal swings
Change all pages and compare traffic to the previous month, since a recent baseline reflects current demand
Change the ten highest-traffic pages first and compare them to the lowest-traffic pages in the set
Change a random half of the pages and compare them with the unchanged half over the same weeks

rubric: A randomised control group of similar pages isolates the change from seasonality and algorithm shifts.
Before/after and year-on-year comparisons carry confounders; hand-picked groups are biased.

items.prompt: A team plans 2,000 programmatic pages that differ only by swapping a city name into identical text for a service business. Which are valid criticisms of the plan? Select all that apply.

options.label: Any templated page is penalised, so programmatic SEO can never work
Thousands of thin pages may dilute crawl attention and bloat the index
City names in URLs are ignored, so the pages cannot rank for local terms
Near-duplicate pages offer little unique value, risking low-quality classification
Pages lacking local detail won't satisfy local intent better than existing results

rubric: Valid concerns are thin duplication, index bloat and missing local value.
Templates are fine if they hold unique data; city terms in URLs do not cause failure.

items.prompt: After a core update, a review site loses 40% of organic traffic. Losses sit almost entirely in affiliate roundups with thin, copied specs; crawl logs, speed and indexation are stable, and original hands-on reviews held steady. Which response is best supported by the evidence?

options.label: Submit a disavow file for all links, since a sitewide link problem explains a segment drop
Wait for the next update to reverse the drop, because core updates are usually temporary
Rebuild the thin roundups with original testing, or prune them, before any technical work
Migrate to a faster host, since stable speed metrics must still be hiding a rendering issue

rubric: The loss is concentrated in thin content while technical signals are stable, pointing to quality.
Distractors chase technical or link causes the data does not support.

items.prompt: A site serves English to the US and UK plus German. Constraints: each audience gets its own version, no duplicate-content confusion, and no forced IP redirects. Which design meets all?

options.label: Separate directories per locale with reciprocal self-referencing hreflang tags plus an x-default
One English URL set for both countries, with hreflang only on the German pages pointing back
Auto-redirect visitors by IP to a locale and canonicalise every version to the US English page
Locale versions at one URL, switched by cookie, so crawlers see a single page per path

rubric: Distinct URLs with complete reciprocal hreflang satisfy all constraints.
Canonicalising to one version or cookie switching hides locales from search engines.

items.prompt: A B2B team can publish 12 articles this quarter. Goal: build authority to eventually rank for a high-difficulty commercial term, with no existing authority. Which plan fits best?

options.label: Publish 12 articles all targeting the commercial term to maximise relevance signals
Skip content and buy links to the commercial page, which is faster than building topical depth
Write one pillar page plus 11 interlinked long-tail articles on lower-difficulty related intents
Publish 12 unrelated trending topics to maximise total impressions across the site

rubric: A cluster with internal links builds topical authority via winnable queries first.
Cannibalising one term, buying links, or scattering topics fails the constraints.

items.prompt: A news site uses infinite scroll; older articles become unreachable to crawlers since content loads on scroll events. Constraint: keep the user experience. Which fix works best?

options.label: Block the feed in robots.txt and rely on the XML sitemap alone for discovery
Provide paginated URLs with crawlable anchor links, updating the address as the user scrolls
Add all older article URLs to the footer so a single page lists thousands of links
Replace the scroll with a button that loads content only through JavaScript click events

rubric: Crawlable paginated URLs keep infinite scroll for users while exposing content.
Click-only loading and sitemaps alone leave discovery weak.

items.prompt: A retailer wants product rich results across 50,000 pages. Constraints: eligibility, no markup that contradicts what users see, low maintenance. Which design fits?

options.label: Generate JSON-LD from the same data source that renders visible price, stock and reviews
Mark up only the top 50 products manually and copy their markup onto similar products
Embed hidden markup with higher prices and reviews than shown to stand out in results
Hand-write JSON-LD per page quarterly, including a fixed aggregate rating on every product

rubric: Generating markup from the same source keeps it accurate and low maintenance.
Hand-written, copied or hidden markup drifts from visible content and breaks guidelines.

items.prompt: A small SaaS has a low budget and may not buy links. It needs earned links from credible sites within six months. Which plan fits every constraint?

options.label: Publish an original dataset from product usage and pitch it to relevant journalists
Sponsor articles on industry blogs without rel attributes so the links pass full value
Swap links with fifty partner sites through a dedicated reciprocal links page on each
Post comments with keyword-rich anchors on high-authority blogs in the niche each week

rubric: Original data gives a linkable asset earned without payment.
Link exchanges, comment spam and undisclosed sponsorship violate link guidelines.

items.prompt: You must plan a domain migration that preserves rankings. Which elements belong in the plan? Select all that apply.

options.label: Blocking the new site in robots.txt for the first month to avoid duplication
A one-to-one 301 map from old URLs to their closest equivalents
Updating internal links, canonicals and sitemaps to the new URLs at launch
A benchmark crawl and rankings snapshot before launch for post-launch comparison
Redirecting every old URL to the new homepage for simplicity

rubric: Mapped redirects, a baseline, and updated internal signals support equity retention.
Blocking the new site or redirecting everything home defeats the migration.

items.prompt: A marketplace has 40,000 expired listings. Some have strong backlinks and still get searches; most have none. Constraints: preserve link equity, avoid soft 404s, help users, keep the sitemap clean. Which design meets all?

options.label: 301 all expired listings to the homepage so every old URL still reaches a live page and passes its link equity there
301 linked or searched listings to their closest category; 410 the rest; drop all from the sitemap
Return 410 for every expired listing immediately, including those with backlinks, and remove them from the sitemap
Keep all expired pages live with a banner and a noindex tag, and leave them in the sitemap so crawlers recheck them

rubric: Relevant redirects keep equity where it exists; 410 handles the rest cleanly.
Homepage redirects create soft 404s; blanket 410 or noindex wastes equity and sitemap hygiene.
